#### Breeding Bird Shapefile

Finally, we need to have a GIS shapefile that tells us the range of the breeding birds, so that genoscape can be clipped properly.  We read this shapefile with the  `st_read()` function from package `sf`. 
See code below. This is easily downloadable from eBird, if you are a subscriber! It was created using the ebirdst function, but downloading a current raster is feasible!

```{r}
breeding<-st_read("~/Dropbox/BGP/Teaching/BZ525_Fall2025/Week5_PopStructure/AMKE_assays/AMKE_data/AMKE/AMKE.range_smooth.sf.WGS84.Ebird.shp") %>% filter(season=="breeding")

#crop<-c(-152.9703,-37.20669,0,68.98193)
breeding_crop <- st_crop(breeding, c(xmin=-152.9703, xmax=-37.20669, ymin=25.2, ymax=68.98193))

```
Plotting the shapefile

```{r}
ggplot() +
  ggspatial::layer_spatial(breeding_crop) +
  theme_bw()
```
## Meta data file for nonbreeding birds
```{r}
new_meta<-read.xlsx("input/SupplementaryTable2.AppendixCH.7172026.xlsx",sheet=1,detectDates = T)  %>% 
  #rename(Sample=indiv) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample,Country_code,State,Location,Latitude,Longitude,CollectionDate,Stage,Contact,SampleTypeExtracted) %>% distinct() %>% arrange(Sample)

read.xlsx("input/SupplementaryTable2.AppendixCH.7172026.xlsx",sheet=1,detectDates = T)  %>% 
  #rename(Sample=indiv) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample,Country_code,State,Location,Latitude,Longitude,CollectionDate,Stage,Contact,SampleTypeExtracted,Alaska:Florida) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  arrange(Sample) %>% 
  mutate(assignment=if_else(Alaska > 0.8,"Alaska",if_else(West > 0.8,"West",if_else(Texas > 0.8 ,"Texas",if_else(East > 0.8, "East",if_else(Florida >0.8, "Florida","Uncertain")))))) %>% group_by(assignment) %>% tally()
```

## Population assignment using rubias

Rubias is an R software program that probabilistically assigns individuals to specific reporting units (i.e. genetic clusters diagnosed in the breeding region). Originally used for fish stock identification, we've co-opted it for bird genoscapes! I've attached the two rubias files you'll need. The known breeder genotypes and the genotypes of the migrating birds. Note, since we don't know where the migrating birds are coming from, we consider them unknown and we are going to use rubias to estimate mixing proportions and probability of assignment to their breeding origin. Thus, we consider the unknown birds a potential *mixture* of individuals from distinct genetic clusters.

Read in this data, and double check that it doesn't have an extra column for whatever reason at the end. 
We ran this is 3 iterations, a first batch of US nonbreeding birds, a second round of genotyping of just Central and South American birds from museums, and a third genotyping session fo southeastern birds.

``` {r}
amke_mix1<-read_delim("input/Rubias/AMKE.groupPlate58.Wint.rubias_input2.rmdup.txt",delim="\t") 

amke_mix2<-read_delim("input/Rubias/AMKE_186SNPgenotypes_str_format.414WintMigr.StateFID.str.rubias2.rename.txt",delim="\t") %>% 
  filter(indiv %in% new_meta$Sample) %>% 
  mutate(collection2="mixture") %>% 
  dplyr::select(-collection) %>% 
  rename(collection=collection2) %>% 
  dplyr::select(sample_type,repunit,collection,indiv,everything()) %>% distinct()


amke_mix3<-read_delim("input/Rubias/AMKE.Plate54_57.Wint.callmap.rubias_input3.txt",delim="\t")
amke_mix_tot<-amke_mix1 %>% full_join(amke_mix2) %>% full_join(amke_mix3) %>% rename(Sample=indiv) %>% filter(Sample %in% new_meta$Sample)
```


#### Organizing and filtering the data

Read in the reference file (597 individuals gentoyped at 182 SNP-type assays) and make sure all fields are correct type. For instance, missing data needs to be coded as NA.
```{r}
## With resident individuals
amke_ref_inclRes<-read_delim("~/Dropbox/BGP/Teaching/BZ525_Fall2025/Week5_PopStructure/AMKE_assays/AMKE_data/AMKE_186SNPgenotypes.breeders.412inds_197Radinds.stateFID.hwe.ped.str.5regionlocation.0_NA.4rubias2.txt",delim="\t")

#amke_ref_inclRes<-read_delim("input/Rubias/AMKE_186SNPgenotypes.breeders.412inds_197Radinds.stateFID.hwe.ped.str.5regionlocation.4rubias2.txt",delim="\t")

## Exclude resident individuals
amke_ref_noRes<-amke_ref_inclRes %>% filter(repunit!="FL") %>% filter(repunit!="TX")

amke_ref2_inclRes<-amke_ref_inclRes %>% mutate_if(is.double,as.integer) 
```

Note, each iteration has failures of some assays. Below we figure out what they (code chunk after this one), and we remove snps not found in 50% of nonbreeding set.

```{r}
#remove SNPs that were not in 50% of the first US nonbreeding bird dataset (amke_mix_US)
amke_ref2_inclRes_US<-amke_ref2_inclRes %>% dplyr::select(-amke_popID54,-amke_popID54.1,-amke_popID92,-amke_popID92.1,-amke_popID93,-amke_popID93.1,-amke_popID60,-amke_popID60.1) 

#remove SNPs that were not in 50% of the Central American and South American US nonbreeding bird dataset (amke_mix_MX)
amke_ref2_noRes<-amke_ref_noRes %>% 
  dplyr::select(-amke_popID104,-amke_popID104.1,-amke_popID94,-amke_popID94.1,-amke_popID93,-amke_popID93.1,-amke_popID106,-amke_popID106.1) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.double,as.integer)
```

Use the code below to ask how many reference individuals there are including residents:

```{r}
dim(amke_ref2_inclRes)
```

#### Read in the nonbreeding (winter and migratory) AMKE data

Here I don't think we need to remove any assays, so I commented out, combine with the reference dataset and filter out again. This is for counting purposes
```{r}
amke_mix_SE2<-amke_ref2_inclRes %>% full_join(amke_mix1) %>% filter(sample_type=="mixture") 

#check number of NAs, remove if over 50%
amke_mix_SE2 %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_NA") %>%
  mutate(pct_NA = round(100 * n_NA / nrow(amke_mix_SE2), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_NA))
```

```{r}
amke_mix_SE3<-amke_mix_SE2 %>% 
  mutate_if(is.double,as.integer)
class(amke_mix_SE3)

amke_mix_US2<-amke_ref2_inclRes %>% full_join(amke_mix2) %>% filter(sample_type=="mixture") %>% filter(indiv %in% new_meta$Sample) 

#check number of NAs, remove if over 50%
amke_mix_US2 %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_NA") %>%
  mutate(pct_NA = round(100 * n_NA / nrow(amke_mix_US2), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_NA))
```

```{r}
amke_mix_US3<-amke_mix_US2 %>% 
  dplyr::select(-amke_popID54,-amke_popID54.1,-amke_popID92,-amke_popID92.1,-amke_popID93,-amke_popID93.1,-amke_popID60,-amke_popID60.1) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.double,as.integer)
class(amke_mix_US3)
```

Use the code below to determine how many migrating individuals we were able to successfully genotype from US: 
```{r}
dim(amke_mix_SE3)
dim(amke_mix_US3)
```

To perform genetic mixing and assignment tests, we use the _infer_mixture function_ in _rubias_. Our data consists of birds caught at multiple banding stations and locations, however, we denote this as just "mixture" in the collection column. This is how it is run with the default options:

For US nonbreeding individuals, we include resident individuals.

```{r}
mix_est.SE <- infer_mixture(reference = amke_ref2_inclRes, mixture = amke_mix_SE3, gen_start_col = 5)
mix_est.US <- infer_mixture(reference = amke_ref2_inclRes_US, mixture = amke_mix_US3, gen_start_col = 5)
```

For non-US nonbreeding individuals, we do not include resident individuals.They seem to rarely move based on banding data (see script 3)

```{r}
amke_mix_MX2<-amke_ref2_noRes %>% full_join(amke_mix3) %>% filter(sample_type=="mixture") 

#check number of NAs, remove if over 50%
amke_mix_MX2 %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_NA") %>%
  mutate(pct_NA = round(100 * n_NA / nrow(amke_mix_MX2), 1)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_NA))
```


```{r}
amke_mix_MX3<-amke_mix_MX2 %>% 
    dplyr::select(-amke_popID104,-amke_popID104.1,-amke_popID94,-amke_popID94.1,-amke_popID93,-amke_popID93.1,-amke_popID106,-amke_popID106.1) %>% 
  mutate_if(is.double,as.integer)
class(amke_mix_MX3)
```

Now run rubias for this dataset.
```{r}
mix_est.MX <- infer_mixture(reference = amke_ref2_noRes, mixture = amke_mix_MX3, gen_start_col = 5)
```


The result comes back as a list of four tidy data frames:

1. mixing_proportions: the mixing proportions. The column pi holds the estimated mixing proportion for each collection.

2. indiv_posteriors: this holds, for each individual, the posterior means of group membership in each collection. Column PofZ holds those values. Column log_likelihood holds the log of the probability of the individuals genotype given it is from the collection. Also included are n_non_miss_loci and n_miss_loci which are the number of observed loci and the number of missing loci at the individual. A list column missing_loci contains vectors with the indices (and the names) of the loci that are missing in that individual. It also includes a column z_score which can be used to diagnose fish that don’t belong to any samples in the reference data base (see below).

3. mix_prop_traces: MCMC traces of the mixing proportions for each collection. You will use these if you want to make density estimates of the posterior distribution of the mixing proportions or if you want to compute credible intervals.

4. bootstrapped_proportions: This is NULL in the above example, but if we had chosen method = "PB" then this would be a tibble of bootstrap-corrected reporting unit mixing proportions.

What we are most interested in is the individual posteriors. We can look at the number of individuals assigned to different genetic clusters and associate those individuals to the meta data we have on them: location, Stage (Breeding, Migratory, or Wintering) and timing (Month, Day and Year).

```{r}
library(splitstackshape) #may not need this because we don't have duplicates

rep_indiv_ests.US <- mix_est.US$indiv_posteriors %>%
  group_by(mixture_collection, indiv, repunit) %>%
  summarise(rep_pofz = sum(PofZ)) %>% spread(repunit,rep_pofz)

rep_indiv_ests.SE <- mix_est.SE$indiv_posteriors %>%
  group_by(mixture_collection, indiv, repunit) %>%
  summarise(rep_pofz = sum(PofZ)) %>% spread(repunit,rep_pofz)

rep_indiv_ests.MX <- mix_est.MX$indiv_posteriors %>%
  group_by(mixture_collection, indiv, repunit) %>%
  summarise(rep_pofz = sum(PofZ)) %>% spread(repunit,rep_pofz) %>% mutate(TX=0.00,FL=0.00)

rep_indiv_ests.tot<-rep_indiv_ests.SE %>% full_join(rep_indiv_ests.US) %>% full_join(rep_indiv_ests.MX) %>% 
  rename(Alaska=AK,Florida=FL,Texas=TX) %>% 
  distinct()

##There are no duplicate individuals in the data- so do not need to split the columns 
rep_indiv_ests.a2<-rep_indiv_ests.tot %>%
  rename(Sample=indiv) %>% 
  filter(Sample %in% new_meta$Sample) %>% 
  left_join(new_meta) %>% 
  dplyr::select(mixture_collection,Sample,Alaska:West,(everything())) %>%
  distinct() 

rep_indiv_ests.a2 %>% filter(Florida>0.8)

```

```{r}
library(writexl)
 rep_indiv_ests.a2 %>% mutate(maxprob= do.call(pmax, c(pick(Alaska:West), na.rm = TRUE)),assignment=if_else(Alaska > 0.8, "Alaska",if_else(East>0.8,"East",if_else(Florida>0.8,"Florida",if_else(Texas>0.8,"Texas",if_else(West>0.8,"West","Uncertain")))))) %>% writexl::write_xlsx("output/Rubias/AMKE.all.rep_indiv_est.inclRES_US.exclRES_MX_result.incl_meta.Appendix2.xlsx")

rep_indiv_ests.a2 %>% mutate(assignment=if_else(Alaska > 0.8, "Alaska",if_else(East>0.8,"East",if_else(Florida>0.8,"Florida",if_else(Texas>0.8,"Texas",if_else(West>0.8,"West","Uncertain")))))) %>% group_by(assignment) %>% tally()
 
filt<- rep_indiv_ests.a2 %>%
  filter(Stage!="Breeding") %>% 
  mutate(maxprob= do.call(pmax, c(pick(Alaska:West), na.rm = TRUE))) %>% 
  mutate(Alaska=if_else(Alaska>.8,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(East=if_else(East>.8,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(Florida=if_else(Florida>.8,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(Texas=if_else(Texas>.8,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(West=if_else(West>.8,1,0)) %>%
  mutate(sum=Alaska+East+Florida+Texas+West) %>% 
  filter(sum==1) %>% #keep only certain inds
  mutate(assignment=if_else(Alaska==1,"Alaska",if_else(West==1,"West",if_else(East==1,"East",if_else(Florida==1,"Florida resident","TX resident"))))) %>% 
  dplyr::select(Sample,Alaska:West,maxprob,assignment,Country_code,State,Location,Latitude,Longitude, CollectionDate,Stage)

write.table(filt,"output/Rubias/AMKE.all.rep_indiv_est.inclRES_US.exclRES_MX.result.filt_certain_withAssignments01.txt",quote=F,sep="\t",row.names=F)


```

uncertain_birds<-read.xlsx("output/Rubias/AMKE.all.rep_indiv_est.inclRES_US.exclRES_MX_result.incl_meta.Appendix2.xlsx",sheet=1,detectDates=T) %>% filter(Sample %notin% assign01$Sample)
uncertain_birds

Where are the uncertain birds located? All over?

```{r}
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
states <- ne_states(country = c("united states of america", "canada", "mexico"), returnclass = "sf")
bb <- c(range(birds$Longitude) + c(-2, 2), range(birds$Latitude) + c(-2, 2))

birds <- rep_indiv_ests.a2 %>% mutate(assignment=if_else(Alaska > 0.8, "Alaska",if_else(East>0.8,"East",if_else(Florida>0.8,"Florida",if_else(Texas>0.8,"Texas",if_else(West>0.8,"West","Uncertain")))))) %>%
  mutate(uncertain = assignment == "Uncertain")

base_map <- list(
  geom_sf(data = world,  fill = "grey95", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2),
  geom_sf(data = states, fill = NA,       color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.1),
  coord_sf(xlim = bb[1:2], ylim = bb[3:4], expand = FALSE),
  theme_minimal(),
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
)

## 1. Density of uncertain birds
p_density <- ggplot() +
  base_map +
  stat_density_2d(data = uncertain_birds, aes(Longitude, Latitude, fill = after_stat(level)),
                  geom = "polygon", alpha = 0.6, bins = 8) +
  geom_point(data = uncertain_birds, aes(Longitude, Latitude), size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", name = "Density") +
  ggtitle(paste0("Uncertain assignments (n = ", nrow(uncertain_birds), ")"))

## 2. Proportion uncertain per 2° cell (controls for sampling effort)
cell <- 2
grid_df <- birds %>% 
  mutate(gx = floor(Longitude / cell) * cell + cell / 2,
         gy = floor(Latitude  / cell) * cell + cell / 2) %>%
  group_by(gx, gy) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), prop_unc = mean(uncertain), .groups = "drop")

p_prop <- ggplot() +
  base_map +
  geom_tile(data = grid_df, aes(gx, gy, fill = prop_unc), width = cell, height = cell, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_text(data = grid_df, aes(gx, gy, label = n), size = 2.3, color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", limits = c(0, 1), name = "Prop.\nuncertain") +
  ggtitle("Proportion of birds with uncertain assignment (cell labels = n sampled)")

p_density
p_prop

ggsave("output/Rubias/AMKE.uncertain_birds_heatmap_version1.png", p, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
I'm going to create one pie plot and place it on a map, for illustration purposes. Alter this at will for what you want to present later for a project:

```{r}
assign<-read_delim("output/Rubias/AMKE.all.rep_indiv_est.inclRES_US.exclRES_MX.result.filt_certain_withAssignments01.txt",delim="\t") %>% 
  distinct()
  
coords <- assign %>% dplyr::select(Longitude, Latitude)

# calculate distance matrix using Haversine distance
dist_matrix <- distm(as.matrix(coords), fun = distHaversine)

# clustering
hclust_groups <- hclust(as.dist(dist_matrix), method = "complete") # complete method here avoids chaining, ensuring all samples in a cluster are within the specified distance of each other. If you want some flexibility you could try "average"

# cut tree at 111.111 km to assign spatial clusters
assign$GroupID <- cutree(hclust_groups, h = 111111)

# create population labels and filter for minimum cluster size
assign <- assign %>%
  mutate(Pop = paste0("Cluster_", GroupID)) %>%
  group_by(Pop) %>%
  #filter(n() > 3) %>%  # keep clusters with ≥4 individuals
  ungroup()  

filt<-assign %>% 
  group_by(Pop) %>% 
  summarise(West=sum(West),East=sum(East),Florida=sum(Florida),Alaska=sum(Alaska),Texas=sum(Texas),meanLat=mean(Latitude),meanLong=mean(Longitude))

filt

```
